item.content:encoded:
The adidas Foundation has opened applications for the Moving for Change 2026 Request for Proposals, a major funding opportunity designed to advance gender equality through Sport for Development initiatives in Eastern Africa.

International non-governmental organizations working in Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, or Uganda are invited to develop and submit joint proposals with locally based Sport for Development organizations. Selected partnerships will receive multi-year financial support to design and implement projects that use sport as a practical platform for promoting gender equality, strengthening opportunities for girls and women, and embedding Sport for Development approaches into institutional strategies and systems.

The application period opened on July 6, 2026, and proposals must be submitted no later than August 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Central European Summer Time. Applications submitted after the deadline or outside the official submission platform will not be considered.

Overview of the Moving for Change Programme

Moving for Change is an adidas Foundation programme that supports international development organizations in integrating sport-based approaches into their broader development work.

Rather than treating sport only as recreation or competition, the programme promotes Sport for Development, commonly abbreviated as S4D. This approach uses structured, inclusive and carefully designed sport activities to help address social challenges and improve development outcomes.

Through Moving for Change, sport may be used as a platform to:

  • Promote gender equality.
  • Increase the participation and leadership of girls and women.
  • Reduce gender-based violence and harassment.
  • Challenge harmful gender norms.
  • Encourage positive and non-violent models of masculinity.
  • Improve access to education, mentorship and economic opportunities.
  • Strengthen social cohesion among divided or marginalized communities.
  • Build trust, confidence, safety and shared belonging.
  • Strengthen the institutional capacity of development organizations.
  • Generate evidence about how sport contributes to sustainable development.

The programme is particularly aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 5: Gender Equality. Applicants must demonstrate how their proposed interventions will use sport intentionally to advance outcomes for girls and women while responding to the realities of the selected community and country.

Key Information at a Glance

The main details of the Moving for Change 2026 opportunity are as follows:

  • Programme name: Moving for Change
  • Lead funder: adidas Foundation
  • Application opening date: July 6, 2026
  • Application deadline: August 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CEST
  • Total funding available: €2,200,000
  • Maximum funding per project: €700,000
  • Project duration: Three years
  • Expected project start: First half of 2027
  • Geographical focus: Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda
  • Thematic focus: Sport for Development contributing to gender equality
  • Application language: English
  • Required partnership: One eligible INGO and one eligible locally based Sport for Development organization
  • Minimum financial co-funding: 10% of the amount requested from the adidas Foundation
  • Minimum allocation to the local S4D partner: 20% of the total project budget

The adidas Foundation expects applicants to be informed of the initial selection outcome by the end of September 2026. Due diligence and contracting are expected to take place during September, with agreements expected to be signed by October 30, 2026.

Funding Available Under Moving for Change 2026

The adidas Foundation has allocated a total of €2.2 million to this Request for Proposals. Each selected project may receive up to €700,000 for implementation over a three-year period.

The Foundation may award less than the maximum amount requested, depending on the project’s scope, budget justification, feasibility, quality and alignment with the programme’s objectives.

Organizations submitting proposals in more than one eligible country must also observe a cumulative funding ceiling. The maximum cumulative amount that one organization may receive under this call is €1.5 million, including applications submitted through its headquarters, affiliated entities and country offices.

Existing adidas Foundation funding awarded to an organization outside this particular call does not count toward the €1.5 million cumulative ceiling.

Mandatory 10% Financial Co-Funding

The lead INGO must provide financial co-funding equal to at least 10% of the amount requested from the adidas Foundation.

For example, an organization requesting the maximum €700,000 must provide at least €70,000 in financial co-funding. The resulting total project budget would therefore be at least €770,000.

The required contribution:

  • Must be a financial contribution.
  • Must be reflected in the overall project budget.
  • Must be provided by the lead INGO.
  • May be mobilized and documented throughout the three-year implementation period.
  • Does not necessarily have to be deposited or spent at the beginning of the project.

In-kind contributions may be included where they are directly connected to the project and appropriately documented. However, in-kind support does not count toward the mandatory 10% financial co-funding requirement.

Countries Covered by the Opportunity

Proposed projects must be implemented in one of the following countries:

  1. Ethiopia
  2. Kenya
  3. Rwanda
  4. Tanzania
  5. Uganda

Each proposal must focus on one country only. Multi-country projects will not be accepted under this call.

An eligible INGO may apply in more than one country, but it must submit a separate application for each country. It may submit no more than one proposal per country of implementation, and its cumulative funding requests must remain within the programme’s funding limits.

Required Partnership Structure

Applications cannot be submitted by one organization acting alone. Every proposal must be jointly developed by:

  1. One eligible international non-governmental organization serving as the lead applicant and grant recipient.
  2. One eligible, nationally based Sport for Development organization serving as the designated strategic and implementation partner.

The quality of this partnership is a central part of the programme. The local Sport for Development partner should not be treated merely as a contractor or downstream service provider. It must participate meaningfully in the design, implementation, learning and capacity-strengthening elements of the project.

Role of the Lead INGO

The lead INGO will be responsible for:

  • Submitting the official application.
  • Receiving and managing the funding.
  • Coordinating overall project implementation.
  • Managing the partnership.
  • Submitting financial and programme reports.
  • Ensuring compliance with the funding agreement.
  • Integrating Sport for Development approaches into its organizational strategies, systems and programmes.
  • Participating in the Moving for Change Community of Practice.
  • Coordinating monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities.
  • Ensuring that safeguarding, governance and financial controls are maintained.

Role of the Local Sport for Development Partner

The local S4D organization will be expected to:

  • Contribute directly to project design.
  • Provide contextual and technical Sport for Development expertise.
  • Co-deliver the proposed activities.
  • Apply established S4D methodologies.
  • Help strengthen the INGO’s institutional capacity.
  • Contribute to safeguarding and implementation quality.
  • Participate in project-level monitoring and learning.
  • Support the long-term uptake of S4D approaches within the lead organization.

The designated S4D partner must receive at least 20% of the total project budget. Applicants may allocate more than 20% where the organization’s responsibilities and contribution justify a higher allocation. There is no requirement that the remaining 80% must be retained by the lead INGO.

Can Additional Partners Participate?

The required application structure consists of one lead INGO and one designated local S4D partner. However, additional organizations may also participate where their involvement strengthens the proposed project.

Additional participants may include:

  • Local civil society organizations.
  • Academic institutions.
  • Research organizations.
  • Technical experts.
  • International organizations.
  • Multilateral institutions.
  • United Nations agencies.
  • Community-based organizations.
  • Government stakeholders, where appropriate and consistent with the programme rules.

United Nations agencies and other multilateral institutions cannot serve as the lead applicant because they are not classified as INGOs under the call. They may nevertheless participate as additional strategic or technical partners.

The designated local S4D organization must still independently demonstrate the required Sport for Development expertise. The expertise cannot be substituted entirely by an additional technical partner.

Who Can Serve as the Lead Applicant?

The lead applicant must be an International Non-Governmental Organization.

For this call, an INGO is defined as a formally registered, non-profit organization that:

  • Operates independently of government control.
  • Conducts activities across at least three countries.
  • Has legal registration in the proposed country of implementation, either directly or through an affiliated country office.
  • Has maintained at least three years of its own operational presence in the country where the proposed project will be implemented.

An organization may be headquartered outside Eastern Africa and still apply. However, having only local implementing partners in an eligible country is not sufficient. The lead organization itself, or its formally affiliated country office, must have a legally recognized presence and at least three years of operational experience in that country.

An informal partnership, memorandum of understanding, fiscal sponsorship or contractual arrangement with a local organization does not, by itself, satisfy the registration requirement.

Lead Applicant Eligibility Requirements

Eligible lead applicants must meet all mandatory legal, organizational, governance, safeguarding, financial and experience requirements.

Legal and Organizational Requirements

The lead organization must:

  • Be a legally registered non-profit entity.
  • Be registered in the proposed country of implementation, directly or through an affiliated country office.
  • Demonstrate at least three years of operational presence in that country.
  • Operate independently of government control.
  • Conduct activities across at least three countries.
  • Remain politically and religiously independent.
  • Submit no more than one application per country.

Political and religious independence means that the organization must not promote political or religious ideologies, participate in political or religious activism, attempt to convert project participants, or restrict access to services to people who support a particular belief or political position.

Relevant Programme Experience

The lead applicant must demonstrate:

  • Experience in programming connected to SDG 5 and gender equality.
  • Experience working with girls and women.
  • Experience serving communities affected by discrimination or exclusion.
  • Interest in using sport as a development tool.
  • Commitment to integrating S4D learning into its broader institutional work.
  • Capacity to participate in a three-year partnership.
  • Ability to engage in monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning processes.
  • Willingness to participate actively in a Community of Practice.

The lead INGO does not necessarily need to be an existing specialist Sport for Development organization. However, it must demonstrate meaningful experience in gender equality programming and a genuine commitment to embedding S4D approaches into its work.

Governance and Safeguarding Requirements

Strong safeguarding and governance systems are mandatory.

The lead organization must have:

  • A documented safeguarding policy or equivalent framework.
  • Safeguarding standard operating procedures.
  • Systems for identifying and managing safeguarding risks.
  • Accessible mechanisms for reporting concerns.
  • Appropriate response and referral procedures.
  • Measures for protecting participant information and communication materials.
  • Transparent governance structures.
  • Effective internal control systems.
  • Procedures for vetting and monitoring downstream recipients of funding.
  • Inclusive and non-discriminatory organizational practices.

Applicants must demonstrate that their policies cover inclusion across characteristics including race, gender, gender identity, social class, sexual orientation, disability, religion, age and ethnicity.

During due diligence, shortlisted organizations may be asked to provide more detailed evidence of their safeguarding, governance, ethics, financial controls and decision-making arrangements.

Eligibility Requirements for the Local S4D Partner

The designated Sport for Development partner must be a nationally based, legally registered non-profit organization in the country where the project will be implemented.

The organization must:

  • Have at least three years of continuous operational presence and programming in the country.
  • Demonstrate substantial Sport for Development expertise.
  • Have experience designing and delivering S4D activities.
  • Apply established or evidence-based S4D methodologies.
  • Provide technical guidance to other organizations.
  • Be capable of strengthening the institutional S4D capacity of the lead INGO.
  • Have sufficient organizational and financial capacity to manage its responsibilities.
  • Participate centrally in project design and implementation.
  • Receive at least 20% of the total project budget.

The local partner does not have to work exclusively in sport. A civil society organization with a broader development mandate may qualify if it can independently demonstrate substantial and relevant Sport for Development experience.

For-profit companies and social enterprises are not eligible to serve as the designated local S4D partner, even where they have a social or sport-related mission.

Financial Capacity Requirement

The amount requested each year cannot exceed 50% of the lead applicant’s most recent audited annual income.

This requirement is applied to the annual value of the requested funding rather than the total three-year project amount.

For example, a €700,000 award distributed over three years would represent approximately €233,333 per year. To request this amount, the organization would need to demonstrate audited annual income of at least approximately €466,666.

Organizations with lower audited annual income may still apply, but they must request a smaller amount that remains within the 50% threshold.

Applicants should therefore review their audited financial statements carefully before deciding the amount to request. An application may otherwise be technically ineligible even where the proposed programme is strong.

Communities the Projects Should Support

Moving for Change projects must primarily support girls and women. Applicants are expected to apply an intersectional approach, recognizing that gender inequality may overlap with other forms of exclusion and discrimination.

Projects may focus on girls and women affected by factors such as:

  • Gender identity and expression.
  • Sexual orientation.
  • Ethnicity or race.
  • Disability.
  • Nationality.
  • Migrant status.
  • Refugee or displacement status.
  • Religion, belief or faith background.

These categories are intended to guide inclusive and context-sensitive programme design rather than create rigid definitions. Applicants should use appropriate local terminology and consider the legal, cultural, social and policy environment of the country and communities involved.

Projects must therefore demonstrate a clear understanding of how overlapping identities may affect access to safe sport, education, economic opportunities, leadership and community participation.

Expected Project Outcomes

Every proposed project must contribute to at least one community-level outcome and both mandatory organizational outcomes.

Community Outcome 1: Reduced Gender-Based Violence and Harassment

Projects may use sport to:

  • Challenge harmful gender norms.
  • Promote gender-transformative practices.
  • Develop positive and non-violent models of masculinity.
  • Create safer spaces for girls and women.
  • Improve understanding of consent, respect and equality.
  • Build the confidence and leadership of participants.
  • Reduce tolerance for violence and harassment.

Community Outcome 2: Increased Access to Opportunities

Projects may support improved access for girls and women to:

  • Education.
  • Mentorship.
  • Leadership development.
  • Employability support.
  • Skills development.
  • Economic opportunities.
  • Professional networks.
  • Community participation.

These activities must be meaningfully connected to Sport for Development. Sport should function as a platform, entry point or engagement mechanism, although the eventual economic opportunities created do not have to be within the sport sector.

Community Outcome 3: Stronger Social Cohesion

Projects may use safe and inclusive sport-based activities to:

  • Build trust among different groups.
  • Reduce community-level violence.
  • Encourage dialogue and cooperation.
  • Promote shared belonging.
  • Increase the participation of marginalized girls and women.
  • Create inclusive community spaces.

Mandatory Organizational Outcome 4

The project must increase the capacity of the lead INGO to design, implement and sustain Sport for Development initiatives independently.

Mandatory Organizational Outcome 5

The project must support the adoption of Sport for Development principles within the INGO’s strategic frameworks, programmes, policies or institutional systems.

Organizational outcomes are expected to be demonstrated primarily at the country level. Applicants may also explain how the project’s learning could influence broader regional or global organizational practice.

Required Project Components

All proposals must include three interconnected components.

Component One: S4D Implementation With a Local Organization

This component should involve the practical delivery of inclusive sport-based activities contributing to gender equality.

Possible activities include:

  • Co-designing interventions with local communities.
  • Delivering structured sport sessions.
  • Creating safe and inclusive participation spaces.
  • Engaging girls and women in leadership roles.
  • Using participant feedback to improve implementation.
  • Working with coaches, families and community leaders.
  • Integrating safeguarding into all sport activities.

Component Two: S4D Capacity Strengthening for the INGO

This component should build the knowledge and practical ability of the lead organization.

Activities may include:

  • Training employees and partners.
  • Providing technical mentoring.
  • Organizing peer learning.
  • Developing S4D implementation tools.
  • Improving safeguarding knowledge.
  • Strengthening gender-transformative coaching.
  • Building inclusive programme-design capacity.
  • Developing guidance for future S4D initiatives.

Component Three: Organizational Learning and S4D Uptake

This component should ensure that learning continues beyond individual project activities.

Possible actions include:

  • Conducting internal learning and reflection sessions.
  • Documenting implementation experiences.
  • Identifying challenges and lessons.
  • Developing organizational tools and policies.
  • Using evidence to strengthen future programming.
  • Integrating S4D principles into strategic planning.
  • Sharing knowledge across country offices or departments.

The three components should be presented as one coherent project model rather than as unrelated activities.

Community of Practice Participation

Selected organizations will participate in the Moving for Change Community of Practice. This learning platform will be facilitated by a Technical and Learning Partner appointed by the adidas Foundation.

The Community of Practice will support:

  • Peer learning among funded organizations.
  • Technical exchanges.
  • Knowledge sharing.
  • Safeguarding guidance.
  • Institutional capacity building.
  • Reflection on implementation challenges.
  • Documentation of effective practices.
  • Portfolio-wide learning.

Each lead organization must nominate at least one employee to serve as its Community of Practice Lead. The expected commitment is approximately 15 to 20 hours per year.

Participation will include:

  • Quarterly virtual peer-learning sessions lasting approximately 90 minutes.
  • Thematic discussions on safe sport and safeguarding.
  • Exchanges on gender-transformative coaching.
  • Sessions on engaging girls and young women.
  • Learning about measuring gender equality outcomes.
  • An annual regional workshop.
  • Contributions to shared knowledge and evidence.

Up to 5% of the total project budget may be allocated to Community of Practice participation, including staff time, peer-learning activities and relevant travel costs.

Budget Development Guidance

Applicants must use the official budget template and clearly explain how requested resources will support implementation.

Important budget rules include:

  • The designated local S4D partner must receive at least 20% of the total project budget.
  • The lead INGO must provide financial co-funding equal to at least 10% of the requested adidas Foundation amount.
  • Indirect cost recovery may represent up to 15% of the requested budget.
  • Up to 5% of the total project funding may support Community of Practice participation.
  • Applicants are encouraged to allocate approximately 5% of the total project budget to monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning.
  • The annual amount requested cannot exceed 50% of the lead organization’s latest audited annual income.
  • The budget must be reasonable, clearly justified and aligned with the proposed activities and responsibilities.

Indirect costs may include eligible organizational expenses such as administrative salaries, office rent, utilities, communication expenses, insurance, office equipment and general operational support.

Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning

Applicants must submit an Indicator Tracking Table as part of the application and explain how progress will be measured.

The programme provides a list of suggested indicators, but applicants may propose additional indicators where necessary. Any additional indicators should be:

  • Clearly defined.
  • Measurable.
  • Relevant to the intervention.
  • Aligned with the intended outcomes.
  • Realistic within the three-year timeframe.

Applicants should clearly connect activities, outputs and outcomes through the project logframe and theory of change.

Strong applications will explain:

  • What changes are expected.
  • Who will experience those changes.
  • How progress will be measured.
  • Which organization will collect and analyze data.
  • How participant feedback will be obtained safely.
  • How learning will influence implementation.
  • How evidence will support institutional S4D uptake.

Approximately 5% of the total project budget should, where appropriate, be allocated to MEAL activities.

Reporting Requirements for Selected Organizations

Selected partners will participate in structured financial, programme and learning reporting throughout the three-year period.

The lead INGO will remain responsible for submitting reports to the adidas Foundation while coordinating information from the local S4D partner.

Expected reporting includes:

  • Annual financial progress reports.
  • Biannual implementation updates.
  • Biannual Indicator Tracking Table updates.
  • Biannual check-in calls with the adidas Foundation.
  • Annual narrative reports.
  • Documentation of achievements and challenges.
  • Lessons learned and implementation reflections.
  • Photographs accompanied by appropriate consent documentation.
  • Stories of change from participants and organizations.

Organizations will not normally be required to submit individual receipts or vouchers with regular reports. However, they must maintain complete, accurate and verifiable financial records and make supporting documents available for audits, spot checks or compliance reviews when requested.

Documents Required for the Application

Applicants must complete a full application and submit all required templates and supporting documents in English.

Project Application Documents

The online application must include:

  • A detailed project proposal.
  • The proposed implementation approach.
  • Information about organizational experience and capacity.
  • An explanation of the community context.
  • Details of the partnership approach.
  • Plans for integrating S4D into organizational systems.
  • A completed draft budget.
  • A project logframe.
  • An implementation schedule.
  • An Indicator Tracking Table.

Organizational Documents

Applicants must also provide:

  • Proof of legal registration.
  • Evidence of non-profit status.
  • A safeguarding policy or equivalent framework.
  • The most recent audited financial statements.

The audited financial statements should include, where available:

  • A statement of financial position or balance sheet.
  • An income statement.
  • A cash-flow statement.

Documents must be submitted in English. An unofficial English translation may be accepted at the initial application stage for proof of registration, but official or certified translations may be required during final selection and due diligence.

Two-Stage Selection Process

Stage One: Full Application Submission

Eligible organizations must complete the official online application and upload all required project and organizational documents before the deadline.

The adidas Foundation will assess the proposal’s eligibility, strategic relevance, partnership quality, design, safeguarding approach, financial alignment and expected results.

Stage Two: Due Diligence

Shortlisted organizations will undergo a detailed due-diligence process.

They may be required to submit:

  • Certified evidence of legal registration.
  • Statutes or bylaws.
  • Governance and oversight arrangements.
  • Organizational structures and organograms.
  • Financial management procedures.
  • Accounting and internal-control systems.
  • Evidence of the ability to track restricted funds.
  • Detailed safeguarding procedures.
  • Reporting and referral mechanisms.
  • Codes of conduct.
  • Ethics policies.
  • Details of senior management and key employees.
  • Authorized signatory information.
  • Additional compliance documentation.

Shortlisting does not automatically guarantee final funding. Final selection will depend on successful completion of due diligence and contracting.

How Proposals Will Be Evaluated

Applications will be assessed according to seven weighted criteria:

  1. Strategic relevance and contextual understanding — 20%
  2. Focus-community engagement and partnership quality — 20%
  3. Project design and feasibility — 20%
  4. Safeguarding — 10%
  5. Outcomes and MEAL readiness — 10%
  6. Community of Practice engagement and change readiness — 10%
  7. Budget and financial alignment — 10%

The three highest-weighted areas collectively account for 60% of the assessment. Applicants must therefore present strong evidence that the intervention responds to a clearly defined local need, has been developed through a credible partnership, and can realistically be implemented within the proposed timeframe and budget.

Safeguarding, monitoring systems, institutional change readiness and financial alignment must also be treated as core proposal elements rather than administrative additions.

Practical Recommendations for Preparing a Competitive Proposal

Organizations preparing an application should begin by confirming technical eligibility. A strong project idea cannot compensate for failure to meet a mandatory registration, operational-presence, financial-capacity or partnership requirement.

Applicants should:

  1. Verify the lead organization’s legal status.
    Confirm that the INGO is legally registered, directly or through an affiliated office, in the proposed country.
  2. Confirm three years of operational presence.
    Evidence should relate to the lead applicant’s own operations rather than activities implemented only through external partners.
  3. Select an experienced local S4D partner.
    The partner should have a documented record of designing and implementing evidence-based Sport for Development initiatives.
  4. Develop the proposal jointly.
    The S4D partner should participate from the design stage rather than being added after the proposal has already been developed.
  5. Build the project around community realities.
    Proposals should reflect the barriers, risks, needs and opportunities faced by girls and women in the specific location.
  6. Create a credible theory of change.
    Clearly show how sport-based activities will lead to outputs, community outcomes and institutional change.
  7. Integrate safeguarding throughout the project.
    Safeguarding should be reflected in activity design, staffing, risk management, participant feedback, communication and reporting.
  8. Explain institutional uptake.
    The application must show how S4D principles will become part of the INGO’s long-term strategies, systems or policies.
  9. Prepare a realistic budget.
    Confirm compliance with the 10% co-funding requirement, 20% S4D allocation, annual-income limit and indirect-cost ceiling.
  10. Demonstrate MEAL readiness.
    Include practical indicators, data-collection responsibilities, baselines, targets and learning mechanisms.
  11. Review all documents before submission.
    Applications submitted outside the official platform, after the deadline or without required documents will not be accepted.

Common Reasons an Organization May Be Ineligible

An organization is likely to be ineligible where:

  • The lead applicant is a national NGO that does not operate across at least three countries.
  • The lead applicant has no legal registration or affiliated country office in the implementation country.
  • Its operational presence exists only through independent local partners.
  • The proposed local S4D partner is a for-profit social enterprise.
  • The local partner lacks substantial S4D experience.
  • The application includes more than one country.
  • More than one proposal is submitted for the same country.
  • The annual funding request exceeds 50% of the lead applicant’s audited annual income.
  • The lead organization cannot provide the required financial co-funding.
  • The S4D partner is allocated less than 20% of the total project budget.
  • The organization lacks documented safeguarding policies.
  • The application is submitted after the deadline.
  • Application materials are not submitted in English.
  • The proposal is not submitted through the official application platform.

How to Apply

Eligible applicants must access the Moving for Change application form and official templates through the adidas Foundation’s RFP webpage.

Applicants should complete the online form, upload the required budget, logframe, implementation schedule, Indicator Tracking Table and organizational documents, and submit the complete application through the official platform.

Applications sent through another channel or received outside the designated application period will not be accepted.

Questions about the application process may be sent to programs@adidasfoundation.org. The recommended email subject line is:

[INGO name] Moving for Change RFP Application Support

Applicants should submit questions early enough to allow time for a response before the application deadline.

Click HERE to apply.

Important Dates

  • Applications opened: July 6, 2026
  • Application deadline: August 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CEST
  • Applicant notification: By the end of September 2026
  • Due diligence and contracting: Expected during September 2026
  • Agreements expected to be signed: By October 30, 2026
  • Expected project commencement: During the first half of 2027

Organizations should not wait until the final day to submit. The application requires several technical documents, partnership decisions, financial calculations and organizational approvals that may take considerable time to finalize.

Conclusion

The adidas Foundation Moving for Change 2026 programme offers a significant opportunity for international development organizations and locally based Sport for Development organizations to build long-term partnerships that advance gender equality in Eastern Africa.

With total available funding of €2.2 million and up to €700,000 available for each three-year project, the initiative can support substantial interventions in Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda.

However, the opportunity has strict organizational, financial and partnership requirements. The lead applicant must qualify as an INGO, have legal registration and at least three years of operational presence in the implementation country, demonstrate experience in gender equality programming, maintain strong safeguarding and governance systems, and work with one qualified local S4D organization.

Successful proposals will go beyond delivering sport activities. They will show how sport can produce measurable improvements for girls and women while also strengthening the lead organization’s long-term capacity to integrate Sport for Development into its policies, systems and programmes.

Eligible organizations should begin partnership planning, financial verification and document preparation well before the August 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CEST deadline.

For more opportunities click HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Communities thrive when young people have access to safe, inclusive, and high-quality spaces where they can learn, grow, build friendships, and participate in sports. Unfortunately, many neighborhoods across the United States continue to face significant challenges due to aging athletic facilities, inadequate recreational infrastructure, and limited investment in youth development spaces. These challenges often reduce opportunities for children and teenagers to engage in organized sports, physical activity, and healthy community interactions. To address this need, The DICK’S Sporting Goods Foundation, in partnership with the Local Initiatives Support Corporation (LISC), has launched the Game On-Community Places to Play Initiative. This impactful grant program is designed to support community-rooted organizations working to renovate or create safe, accessible, and inclusive youth sports facilities in underserved communities throughout the United States. Through this initiative, eligible organizations can receive grant funding ranging from $50,000 to $100,000, along with valuable technical assistance to help successfully implement renovation projects that will benefit local youth for years to come.

If your organization is committed to expanding access to quality sports and recreational spaces for young people, this funding opportunity provides the financial support needed to make lasting improvements in your community.

Application Deadline: August 15, 2026

About the Game On-Community Places to Play Initiative

The Game On-Community Places to Play Initiative is part of the broader Game On program, a collaborative effort between The DICK’S Sporting Goods Foundation and LISC to improve recreational opportunities for children and youth across America.

Recognizing the critical role that sports play in promoting physical health, teamwork, leadership, confidence, and community engagement, the initiative focuses on ensuring that every child—regardless of where they live—has access to safe and well-maintained athletic facilities.

Rather than simply funding construction projects, the program supports organizations deeply rooted in their communities that understand local needs and are committed to creating long-term positive impact through youth sports.

In addition to financial support, selected organizations receive technical assistance to strengthen project planning, implementation, and long-term sustainability.

Grant Overview

Grant Detail Information
Program Game On-Community Places to Play Initiative
Funding Organizations The DICK’S Sporting Goods Foundation and LISC
Opportunity Type Community Grant
Grant Amount $50,000–$100,000
Location United States
Eligible Applicants Non-profit community-based organizations
Funding Requirement 1:1 Matching Funds Required
Project Focus Youth sports facility creation and renovation
Application Deadline August 15, 2026

Purpose of the Initiative

The primary goal of the initiative is to improve the:

  • Quality of community athletic facilities
  • Safety of youth sports environments
  • Accessibility of recreational spaces
  • Availability of sports infrastructure in underserved neighborhoods
  • Opportunities for organized youth sports participation

The program seeks to remove barriers that prevent young people from participating in sports by investing in facilities that are welcoming, functional, and accessible to the entire community.

What the Grant Supports

Funding is available for projects that create or renovate multi-use indoor and outdoor youth sports facilities.

Projects may include improvements to facilities used for:

  • Basketball
  • Baseball
  • Softball
  • Soccer
  • Football
  • Tennis
  • Lacrosse
  • Volleyball
  • Other organized youth sports

Eligible projects should demonstrate that the facility will be actively used by local youth and remain accessible to the broader community.

Funding Available

Successful applicants may receive grants ranging from:

  • $50,000
  • Up to $100,000

A key requirement of the program is that applicants provide a 1:1 funding match.

For example:

  • A $50,000 grant requires a $50,000 match.
  • A $100,000 grant requires a $100,000 match.

Matching funds demonstrate organizational commitment and help maximize the impact of the investment.

Technical Assistance

Beyond financial support, selected organizations receive technical assistance designed to strengthen project implementation.

Support may help organizations with:

  • Project planning
  • Facility development
  • Community engagement
  • Long-term sustainability
  • Project management
  • Best practices for successful implementation

This additional support helps ensure funded projects create meaningful and lasting benefits.

Eligible Projects

Projects should focus on:

  1. Renovating existing athletic facilities.
  2. Creating new multi-use sports spaces.
  3. Improving safety and accessibility.
  4. Expanding community access.
  5. Supporting organized youth sports participation.

Facilities should encourage regular community use and provide opportunities for children and youth from diverse backgrounds.

Who Can Apply?

The initiative welcomes applications from organizations that are deeply connected to the communities they serve.

Eligible applicants include:

  • Non-profit community-based organizations.
  • Youth-serving non-profit organizations.
  • Community development organizations.
  • Schools working in partnership with local non-profit organizations.
  • Local parks and recreation departments collaborating with non-profit partners.

Who Is Not Eligible?

The following organizations are not eligible:

  • Universities.
  • Colleges.
  • College campuses.
  • Organizations that do not meet the non-profit eligibility requirements.
  • Projects located outside the United States.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must:

  • Be a registered non-profit organization.
  • Lead a youth sports facility renovation or creation project.
  • Serve low-to-moderate income communities.
  • Demonstrate meaningful community access to the facility.
  • Support organized youth sports.
  • Provide a required 1:1 funding match.
  • Meet all requirements outlined in the Request for Proposals.

Selection Considerations

Although complete evaluation criteria are outlined in the Request for Proposals (RFP), successful applications are expected to demonstrate:

  • Strong community impact.
  • Organizational capacity.
  • Sustainable project planning.
  • Commitment to youth development.
  • Broad community access.
  • Safe and inclusive facility design.
  • Effective partnerships.
  • Readiness to implement the project.

Benefits of the Grant

Organizations selected under the initiative will benefit from:

Financial Support

  • Grants between $50,000 and $100,000.
  • Funding for facility renovation or development.
  • Support for long-term community infrastructure improvements.

Organizational Growth

Recipients will gain:

  • Technical assistance from experienced professionals.
  • Increased organizational capacity.
  • Stronger community partnerships.
  • Greater visibility within the community.

Community Impact

Funded projects can:

  • Expand youth sports opportunities.
  • Improve public recreational infrastructure.
  • Increase physical activity among children.
  • Promote healthier lifestyles.
  • Foster teamwork, leadership, and inclusion.
  • Create safer environments for youth engagement.

Why Organizations Should Apply

Many communities lack safe and modern athletic spaces where young people can participate in sports and build lifelong skills.

The Game On-Community Places to Play Initiative offers organizations the opportunity to transform outdated facilities into vibrant community assets that support youth development, encourage healthy lifestyles, and strengthen neighborhoods.

For organizations already committed to serving young people, this grant can significantly accelerate facility improvements while creating lasting social impact.

How to Apply

Interested organizations should carefully review the official Request for Proposals (RFP) before beginning their application.

Applicants should ensure they:

  1. Confirm organizational eligibility.
  2. Review all selection criteria.
  3. Prepare documentation demonstrating community need and project readiness.
  4. Secure the required matching funds.
  5. Complete and submit the application before the deadline.

Apply via email here: Sportsandyouthdevelopment@lisc.org

For more information about this application click HERE

 

Conclusion

The Game On-Community Places to Play Initiative 2026 represents an outstanding funding opportunity for community-based organizations dedicated to improving youth sports infrastructure in underserved neighborhoods across the United States. By combining grants of up to $100,000 with technical assistance, the initiative empowers local organizations to create safe, accessible, and inclusive athletic spaces where young people can thrive. Whether renovating an aging basketball court, upgrading a community soccer field, or developing a new multi-use sports facility, this program provides the resources needed to create lasting community impact. Eligible organizations serving low-to-moderate income communities should take advantage of this opportunity by preparing a strong proposal and submitting their application before the August 15, 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Nonprofit organizations looking to improve their long-term sustainability and organizational effectiveness now have an exciting funding opportunity through the Capacity Building Grants program. Designed to help organizations strengthen their internal systems, leadership, infrastructure, and overall effectiveness, these grants provide one-time funding ranging from $100,000 to $250,000.

Rather than funding ongoing operational expenses or recurring program costs, Capacity Building Grants invest in the internal development of organizations so they can achieve greater impact over the long term. Whether your organization needs stronger leadership, improved technology, enhanced fundraising strategies, better data systems, or innovative operational improvements, this funding opportunity is designed to help build lasting organizational capacity.

Applications are currently open, and eligible organizations are encouraged to submit proposals before the deadline.

What Are Capacity Building Grants?

Capacity Building Grants are one-time investments that help nonprofit organizations improve their internal capabilities, allowing them to better achieve their mission and expand their impact over time.

Instead of focusing solely on delivering programs, these grants recognize that strong organizations require equally strong internal systems, effective leadership, sound financial planning, efficient operations, and sustainable organizational strategies.

By investing in these critical organizational foundations, nonprofits become more resilient, adaptable, and better positioned to serve their communities for years to come.

Funding Amount

Successful applicants may receive:

  • One-time grants ranging from $100,000 to $250,000

These funds are intended to support strategic organizational improvements rather than recurring annual funding.

Application Timeline

Organizations interested in applying should carefully note the official application period.

Applications Open:

  • July 13, 2026

Application Deadline:

  • August 13, 2026

Applicants are encouraged to complete the eligibility quiz and review the application materials before preparing their proposal.

Purpose of the Capacity Building Grants

The program exists to help organizations strengthen their internal effectiveness in ways that produce long-lasting organizational improvements.

Rather than supporting day-to-day operational costs alone, these grants focus on helping organizations:

  • Improve organizational sustainability
  • Strengthen leadership and governance
  • Modernize systems and technology
  • Increase operational efficiency
  • Build stronger financial management
  • Expand strategic planning capacity
  • Improve organizational resilience
  • Position themselves for long-term growth

The Foundation specifically supports organizations that can clearly demonstrate:

  • A significant organizational capacity challenge
  • Why addressing this challenge is essential now
  • How a one-time investment will create lasting improvements
  • How the investment aligns with the Foundation’s strategic priorities

What Makes a Strong Capacity Building Grant Proposal?

Applicants should clearly explain every aspect of their proposed investment.

A competitive proposal should address the following areas:

1. Clearly Define the Organizational Need

Organizations should explain:

  • The exact organizational challenge they face
  • Why this issue limits their effectiveness
  • Why addressing this issue is essential

Rather than describing broad goals, applicants should identify one clearly defined organizational capacity need.

2. Explain Why the Investment Matters Now

Reviewers want to understand why the organization requires support at this stage of its development.

Strong applications explain:

  • Organizational growth challenges
  • New opportunities requiring additional capacity
  • Existing barriers preventing greater impact
  • Why immediate investment is necessary

3. Demonstrate Long-Term Sustainability

Since these are one-time grants, organizations should explain how improvements will continue after grant funding ends.

Examples include:

  • Permanent technology improvements
  • Sustainable staffing structures
  • Improved fundraising capacity
  • Stronger governance systems
  • Long-term operational efficiencies

4. Present a Detailed Implementation Plan

Applicants should provide:

  • A realistic budget
  • Project activities
  • Key milestones
  • Implementation timeline
  • Expected organizational outcomes

The proposal should clearly connect each funded activity to measurable organizational improvements.

5. Explain Expected Outcomes

Applicants should describe what will improve after the project.

Possible outcomes include:

  • Better organizational performance
  • Increased financial sustainability
  • Improved staff capacity
  • Enhanced service delivery
  • Stronger partnerships
  • Better decision-making through data
  • Increased operational efficiency

6. Demonstrate Alignment with Foundation Priorities

Organizations should clearly explain how the proposed investment supports the Foundation’s strategic priorities.

Reviewers should be able to understand:

  • The organization’s mission
  • Its community impact
  • The relationship between the proposed investment and the Foundation’s goals

Applicants are encouraged to assume reviewers may be learning about the organization for the first time and therefore provide sufficient organizational background.

Eligible Types of Capacity Building Projects

The Foundation welcomes a broad range of organizational capacity-building initiatives.

Examples include the following.

1. Staffing, Leadership and Organizational Culture

Funding may support efforts to strengthen:

  • Staff development
  • Leadership capacity
  • Executive coaching
  • Board governance
  • Organizational culture
  • Workforce planning
  • Leadership succession

2. Financial Health and Flexible Funding

Organizations may seek support for initiatives that improve financial sustainability, including:

  • Fundraising systems
  • Revenue diversification
  • Business model development
  • Financial planning
  • Financial resilience
  • Flexible organizational support

3. Internal Systems and Operations

Organizations can improve their internal infrastructure through investments such as:

  • Administrative improvements
  • Shared service models
  • Technology upgrades
  • Artificial Intelligence (AI) innovation
  • Digital transformation
  • Workflow improvements
  • Operational modernization

4. Data and Evaluation

Funding may be used to strengthen organizational learning through:

  • Data collection systems
  • Performance measurement
  • Evaluation frameworks
  • Data-informed decision making
  • Organizational learning systems

5. Strategic Planning

Organizations may receive support to develop stronger organizational direction through:

  • Strategic planning
  • Long-term organizational vision
  • Goal setting
  • Organizational assessments
  • Future planning

6. Program Enhancement and Innovation

Organizations may test new approaches through:

  • Pilot projects
  • Time-bound innovation initiatives
  • Expansion of public-facing services
  • New program models
  • Community-responsive innovations

The Foundation encourages thoughtful experimentation that strengthens organizational impact.

7. Communications, Partnerships and Community Engagement

Funding may also support efforts to improve:

  • Public engagement
  • Community outreach
  • Strategic communications
  • Cross-sector partnerships
  • Collaboration with nonprofit organizations
  • Civic partnerships
  • Business partnerships
  • Public education initiatives

The Foundation notes that while it does not fund lobbying, it may support strategic advocacy, education, and other policy engagement activities that do not constitute lobbying.

Additional Resources for Applicants

Before submitting an application, organizations are encouraged to take advantage of several support resources, including:

  • Preview the application form
  • Review the eligibility quiz
  • Visit the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) page
  • Contact the grantee help desk
  • Attend an in-person or virtual “Ask the Impact Officer” session during the summer

These resources can help applicants better understand eligibility requirements, proposal expectations, and the application process.

Click HERE to read more.

Why Organizations Should Apply

Many nonprofit organizations focus heavily on delivering services while postponing investments in their internal capacity due to limited funding.

Capacity Building Grants recognize that lasting community impact depends on strong organizations with effective leadership, modern systems, financial resilience, and strategic planning.

This funding provides organizations with an opportunity to invest in the infrastructure that supports long-term mission success. Whether the need involves leadership development, operational improvements, technology modernization, data systems, fundraising, or strategic planning, these grants help nonprofits build stronger foundations for future growth and increased community impact.

Organizations that clearly demonstrate how a one-time investment will produce sustainable organizational improvements are encouraged to apply before the application deadline.

Click HERE to start your application.

Conclusion

The Capacity Building Grants program offers a valuable opportunity for nonprofit organizations seeking to strengthen their internal capacity and position themselves for long-term success. With grants ranging from $100,000 to $250,000, organizations can invest in leadership, technology, financial sustainability, strategic planning, operations, communications, and innovation that will continue delivering benefits well beyond the grant period. Applicants should focus on presenting a well-defined organizational need, a realistic implementation plan, measurable outcomes, and a strong connection between the proposed investment and the Foundation’s strategic priorities. Interested organizations should ensure they complete their applications before August 13, 2026.
